title: Keyv and Cacheable npm supply-chain worm
summary: Source-backed emergency lead for the August 4, 2026 compromise of Keyv, Cacheable, and community-spread npm packages. The package list is refreshed separately from the public Wiz IOC feed; this record preserves the initial independently reported versions and is not a final SecOpsAI verdict.
detection_rationale: Independent research reports describe a common payload across the Keyv/Cacheable package family and subsequent community-spread releases.
Reported releases add setup.mjs, Math_Symbol.js or math_init.js and an npm preinstall hook; the exact artifact must still be collected and inspected by SecOpsAI.
The public package list is an external lead. A local dependency reference is not required to create or prioritize the investigation.
remediation: Audit package-lock.json, pnpm-lock.yaml, yarn.lock, node_modules, CI caches, and package proxies for every affected package/version in the current source list.

Treat a confirmed installation as a potential credential exposure. Isolate the host, preserve evidence, rotate npm, GitHub, cloud, SSH, CI/CD, and developer-tool credentials, and rebuild from a verified clean lockfile.
Hunt for the source-backed domains, file names, hashes, user-agent, and GitHub repository description indicators before making a final impact statement.
